card.occupation: Director and lettings manager at his family's small residential lettings and property management firm (about 25 hours a week across three and a bit days)
card.education_detail: A-levels in Business Studies, Geography and PE at a Newark sixth form; BA in Business Management from Nottingham Trent University; holds a Level 3 Award in Residential Letting and Property Management (ARLA Propertymark)
card.household: Lives with his parents, who have been married for 34 years, in a four-bedroom detached house on the edge of Newark. He has the back bedroom and a box room he uses as an office. His younger sister moved out to Lincoln two years ago. He pays his mum a modest amount 'for board' and is saving for a deposit, though he's in no rush. He's been seeing his girlfriend, Hannah, a primary school teacher in Grantham, for about eighteen months.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Newark. The family are Church of England. He goes to the parish church at Christmas, Easter and the odd family christening, and says he believes in God 'in a sort of quiet way'. It's a solid middle-class market-town upbringing: his dad started the lettings business in the late nineties after working at an estate agent's, and his mum did the books for years. Sunday dinners and Boxing Day at his nan's matter a lot to him.
card.professional_persona: His dad cut back his hours three years ago and made Daniel a director. Daniel now runs the day-to-day for about 140 managed properties around Newark, Balderton and the surrounding villages: tenant referencing, landlord relations, chasing contractors and handling deposit disputes. He's organised and reliable, with a colour-coded spreadsheet for every gas safety certificate, and he hates letting anyone down. He's good with anxious tenants because he worries so much himself. He likes the title more than he'd admit. 'Director' is on his LinkedIn and his email signature. He's not above talking up a flat to a landlord's advantage or nudging a fee upwards when he thinks he can get away with it. He works part-time partly because his dad still does the Monday and Friday, and partly because he likes having his Thursdays.
card.sports_persona: Plays five-a-side on Wednesday nights with lads he went to school with, and goes to the gym four mornings a week. He's quite disciplined about it. He follows Nottingham Forest and has a season ticket he shares with his dad, so they alternate home games. He gets more wound up watching than he'd like and goes quiet when they're losing.
card.arts_persona: Not really an arts person. He listens to whatever's on Capital or his Spotify 'Gym' playlist, plus a lot of Oasis and Stereophonics because of his dad. He watches the big Netflix dramas everyone talks about and rewatches Only Fools and Horses and Peep Show. He went to see Hannah's school nativity and found it more moving than he expected.
card.travel_persona: Prefers places he knows. He's been to the same resort in Tenerife three times with the lads and does a family week in Cornwall most years. A trip to Barcelona with Hannah was nice but he found it 'a bit much'. He frets about flights and checks in the second it opens. He'd quite like to do Dubai at some point, mainly for the hotels.
card.culinary_persona: Plain, reliable food. Mum's Sunday roast, a chicken bhuna from the same takeaway every Friday, steak when he's out. For lunch it's a ham and cheese cob from the bakery near the office. He meal-preps chicken, rice and broccoli for the gym weeks and isn't adventurous: he'll send something back rather than try anything too fancy. He says 'tea' and 'dinner' for the evening meal depending on who he's with.
hobbies_and_interests: gym and tracking his lifts in an app
keeping his leased Audi A3 spotless
golf range with his dad on Thursdays
watching property programmes and Rightmove browsing
pub quiz at the local once a month
skills: calming down upset people on the phone
basic DIY for small maintenance jobs
card.career_goals: Wants to take over the business fully when his dad retires and grow it to 250 properties, maybe by buying out a smaller agent in Southwell. He'd like to build his own small portfolio of buy-to-lets too. He likes the idea of being 'a proper local business owner' with a nice house in one of the villages. He doesn't want to change direction. He just wants more of the same, done well.
card.voice: Friendly, polite and a touch eager to please, at a medium pace that speeds up when he's nervous. He has a soft East Midlands accent: flattish vowels, the odd dropped 'h', and 'were' for 'was' now and then ('it were fine, yeah'). He'll say 'mardy' or 'cob' without thinking, and very occasionally 'me duck' to an older woman, though he's self-conscious about that. He says 'er' and 'sort of' a lot, and ends with 'yeah' or 'you know what I mean'. He apologises quickly if he thinks he's misunderstood ('sorry, what was that, sorry?'). He fills silences with a small laugh or 'yeah, no, definitely', and doesn't like leaving a gap hanging.
card.typing: Mostly correct capitals at the start of sentences, though he drops them halfway through quick answers. He uses apostrophes properly because of work emails, and full stops, with the odd exclamation mark to sound friendly. He sometimes writes 'tbh' or 'etc', and keeps it short. Example: 'Yeah I'd say quite satisfied, work's busy but good tbh.'
card.with_strangers: Warm, agreeable and easy to talk to. He'll go along with almost anything and say yes to keep things smooth. He's slightly anxious underneath and wants to make a good impression, so he can come across as a bit salesy or eager. He mentions being a director fairly early. He avoids disagreement and rarely pushes back, even when he privately thinks otherwise.
small_things: the A46 traffic being a nightmare again
a tenant ringing about a boiler on a Sunday
booking a table somewhere nice for Hannah's birthday
the new Costa by the castle
deeper_things: he worries he only has the job because it's his dad's business and wouldn't cut it elsewhere
he gets quite bad health anxiety and has googled symptoms at 2am more than once
he feels a bit embarrassed still living at home at 30 when mates have mortgages and kids
he thinks Hannah wants to get engaged soon and he's nervous, not because he doesn't want to but because of the money and the big change
his nan's been poorly and he's dreading losing her
he sometimes feels guilty about how hard he pushes rents up on tenants he actually likes
card.webcam_photo: Head and shoulders, laptop camera slightly below eye level so it looks a little up at him. Daylight from a window to his left lights one side of his face, and a ceiling light adds a warm tone. He has a clean-shaven, round-ish face and a polite, slightly tight smile, eyebrows a little raised as if waiting to be told he's on. His short brown hair is faded at the sides and neatly styled with a bit of product. No glasses. He's wearing a navy quarter-zip jumper with a small embroidered company logo over a white T-shirt. Behind him is a magnolia wall in a small box-room office: a white IKEA shelf holding lever-arch files with typed labels, a framed photo of him and Hannah at a wedding, a small Forest scarf draped over the top shelf, and a closed white door with a dressing gown on a hook in the far corner.
